def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    # Ensure we only consider bins with sufficient capacity
    valid_remaining = np.where(remaining >= 0, remaining, -np.inf)
    # Prioritize bins with smaller remaining space (closer to full)
    # Use negative because we want higher priority for smaller remaining space
    priorities = -valid_remaining
    # Handle bins that cannot fit the item by setting their priority to a very low value
    priorities[remaining < 0] = -np.inf
    return priorities

        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    loads = np.zeros_like(bins)
    valid_bins = bins > 0
    loads[valid_bins] = (bins[valid_bins] - item) / bins[valid_bins]
    loads[~valid_bins] = 0

    # We'll compute how much space remains in each bin

    # Use inverse of normalized remaining capacity as priority (higher priority for more room)
    priority_scores = np.zeros_like(bins)

    mask = valid_bins & (remaining_capacity >= item)
    # For bins that can fit the item, assign higher priority based on remaining capacity
    # Normalize by bin capacity to avoid bias towards larger bins
    normalized_remaining = remaining_capacity[valid_bins] / bins[valid_bins]

    # Scale so that bins with more room have higher priority
    # Reverse the score so that higher remaining capacity gives higher priority
    priority_scores[mask] = remaining_capacity[mask]  # Higher remaining capacity = higher priority
    # Bins that cannot fit the item get lower priority (set to 0)
    priority_scores[~mask] = 0
    return priority_scores
